title: Morphs, Native Heights, Decoded Type, Swipes & Declarative Commands
description: View Transitions morphing, calc-size() auto-height, a decode-on-hover type effect, swipe-to-reveal actions, and the new Invoker Commands API.

drops.title: Shared-Element Morph
drops.description: Tap a card and the browser morphs it into a full detail view via document.startViewTransition().
drops.concept: Uses the View Transitions API's view-transition-name property to make a card's image and title fluidly morph into a full-page detail view instead of just crossfading — a technique that used to require a native-app framework.
drops.source: MDN View Transition API + vtbag.dev shared-element guide

interaction.mouse: Click a card to morph into detail view, click back to morph out

drops.title: calc-size() Auto-Height Panels
drops.description: Native <details> accordion panels that animate to their true intrinsic height with pure CSS.
drops.concept: Historically, animating to height:auto required JS to measure content or a max-height hack. calc-size(auto, size) on the native ::details-content pseudo-element lets the browser animate to the real measured height, with name="" grouping panels into a mutually-exclusive accordion natively.
drops.source: Chrome for Developers · "Animate to height: auto" guide

interaction.click: Toggles the accordion panel with a real height animation

drops.title: Text Decode Reveal
drops.description: Headlines scramble through random glyphs before settling on the real letters, left to right.
drops.concept: A staple 'hacker terminal' effect: each character cycles through a random glyph set on a staggered delay before locking to its real value, reading like a signal resolving out of noise. One instance also auto-triggers once via IntersectionObserver on scroll-into-view.
drops.source: Classic CodePen "Text Scramble Effect" technique (soulwire & community variants)

interaction.mouse: Hover a headline to trigger the decode animation
interaction.touch: Tap triggers the same scramble-to-reveal animation

drops.title: Swipe-to-Reveal Actions
drops.description: Drag a row left to reveal archive/delete actions with rubber-band resistance and a spring settle.
drops.concept: An iOS Mail-style interaction: dragging a list row past the reveal threshold snaps it open to show contextual actions; dragging past the edges resists with rubber-band easing instead of moving 1:1, and releasing anywhere snaps to a clean open or closed rest state.
drops.source: iOS Mail / Android Wear swipe-to-reveal pattern + Motion.dev spring-physics swipe tutorial

interaction.mouse: Click-drag a row left to reveal actions
interaction.touch: Full touch drag support with the same rubber-band physics

drops.title: Invoker Commands API
drops.description: A popover menu, a toast, and a modal dialog wired declaratively with command / commandfor — no JS listeners.
drops.concept: The Invoker Commands API adds command and commandfor attributes to buttons so they can open/close popovers and dialogs (toggle-popover, show-popover, hide-popover, show-modal, close) entirely declaratively, with the browser handling focus trapping and top-layer stacking.
drops.source: MDN Invoker Commands API & CSS-Tricks writeup

interaction.mouse: Click each trigger button to open its popover/toast/dialog
interaction.click: Menu items and dialog buttons close via command="close"/"hide-popover"
